The proposed answer, G(g, g+b) = b, cannot be correct.

Any set of n distinct integers has diameter at least n−1, so G(g, g+b) ≥ g+b−1. This is larger than b whenever g ≥ 2. The solution notices this contradiction itself, then guesses b anyway with no derivation.

A quick check with b = 1 confirms the problem. The set {0, 1, …, g} has g+1 elements. Difference d occurs g+1−d ≤ g times, so it is a valid g-Golomb ruler of diameter g. Hence G(g, g+1) = g, not 1.

I did not derive the correct general formula, but the answer b is ruled out by the lower bound.

VERDICT: REJECT
